newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo gold futures end higher as yen slips.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo gold futures end higher as yen slips.

text.p: Tokyo yen-based gold futures rose to end at the upper side of the day's range in buoyant trade on Monday, supported by the yen's further weakness against the dollar, traders said.

TOCOM's most-active August 1997 gold futures settled 11 yen higher at 1,388 yen per gram. The spot October contract expired at noon at 1,398 yen, up four yen with 1,801 lots of deliveries, while others finished seven to 11 yen firmer.
A spreading view that the yen would weaken further against the dollar encouraged private investors to buy distant months after liquidating longs in nearby months, they said.
The dollar rose to a 42-month high of 113.96 yen on Monday.
Bullion was quoted at $382.95/383.25 per ounce at the Tokyo close, against $382.55/383.05 in New York on Friday.
Short-covering by trade houses helped spot gold gain later in the Asian hours. One trader said, however, that recent weakness in spot platinum could cap further rises in spot gold.

TOCOM platinum futures were mostly firmer. Benchmark August platinum settled seven yen higher at 1,392 yen. The spot October contract expired at noon, down by eight yen with 1,199 lots delivered. Other prices ranged from four to eight yen firmer.
One trader said sentiment in platinum was bearish relative to that of gold due to weak physical demand and bearish technical factors.

Traders said private investors still held a large proportion of the long positions in the platinum-gold spread on TOCOM, and platinum futures could dip to a discount to gold futures as expected long-liquidation could pressure the market.
Silver and palladium futures were mixed. Benchmark August silver finished 1.4 yen per 10 grams higher at 182.8 yen.
Benchmark August palladium was down one yen at 426 yen.
